description.text: Build normal according to the displacement. Or use the normal map if not set.
The set of channels to use as the displacement map source.
Detect changes in the height of the displaced samples. The smaller the threshold, the higher the amount of tessellation.
The length in pixels of the subdivision polygon edges. No polygons are generated beyond this threshold.

Edges larger than this get subdivided automatically, edges smaller than this get subdivided based on the normal threshold and the displace threshold. The smaller the threshold, the higher the amount of tessellation.
The number of times that the polygons subdivision is applied.

Select the polygon subdivision mode:
  • uniform - uniform polygon tessellation.
  • screen - view dependent tessellation, ensures no new triangles are generated once a certain screen size has been reached.
  • adaptive - tessellate according to the displaced geometry complexity.

Detect changes in the normal orientation of the displaced samples. A value of 0.0 indicates normals with the same orientation. A value of 90.0 indicates orthogonal normals. The smaller threshold, the higher the amount of tessellation.

impulse:	no filtering - each output pixel equals some input pixel
linear:	linear interpolation between pixels
cubic:	smooth interpolation between pixels
Keys:	cubic a=.50, approximates sinc (*)
Simon:	cubic a=.75, continuous 2nd derivative (*)
Rifman:	cubic a=1.0, lots of sharpening (*)
Mitchell:	mix of sharpening and smoothing (*+)
Parzen:	approximating B-spline (+)
notch:	hides moiré patterns (+)
Lanczos4:	good for scaling down (*)
Lanczos6:	good for scaling down with some sharpening (*)
sinc4:	good for scaling down with a lot of sharpening (*)
(*) has negative lobes, can produce values that are outside the range of the input pixels.
(+) not interpolatory, changes pixels even when no movement.
The size of the filter used when sampling the input image.

Set how to expand the normal input.

none - 	XYZ
XY - 	2*XY-1
XYZ - 	2*XYZ-1
An overall multiplier that scales the amount of displacement at each vertex.

description.plain_text: This shader adds geometric details to surfaces at rendering time. It locally displaces the geometry in the direction of the surface normal. The displacement input is used to modulate the amplitude of the deformation. The shader can compute the local surface normal after the displacement, or retrieve it from the normal input.
description.text:
This shader adds geometric details to surfaces at rendering time.
It locally displaces the geometry in the direction of the surface normal.
The displacement input is used to modulate the amplitude of the deformation.
The shader can compute the local surface normal after the displacement,
or retrieve it from the normal input.
